entry.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
entry.summary: Microsoft published the technical architecture of ARTEX, an AI framework in wide use since July 2026 that runs cyberattacks via specialized agents with minimal human involvement. State-backed groups from China and North Korea and criminal organizations are using it; Microsoft recommends deception-based defenses like honeypots and fake success signals.

entry.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
entry.summary: Nvidia instructed partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to four Southeast Asian countries under new US export controls targeting Chinese cloud access. Dealers are seeking buyers for thousands of B300 chips amid what one cloud executive calls chaos, with loans and major deals at risk.

entry.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
entry.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority says Meta declined its request for joint pre-launch testing of the Muse personal AI agent, which began rolling out in the UK this week. The FCA warned of potential new attack vectors from autonomous agents operating in financial contexts.

entry.title: 42 state AGs are trying to stop Character.AI from selling users’ chats
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is moving to block Character.AI from auctioning chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts, including 2.1 million belonging to minors, during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy. Disney bought some assets and hired the CEO in October after the company filed for bankruptcy.

entry.title: Dozens of court cases in England and Wales affected by undisclosed AI use in 2026
entry.summary: A Guardian investigation found at least 25 court cases in England and Wales this year affected by undisclosed AI use, including AI-generated witness statements, fabricated case law, and nonexistent statutes. Judges have complained about unacceptable hallucination-driven misuse by lawyers, police, and claimants.

entry.title: Former OpenAI researcher says the Riemann proof matters less than the fact that an AI system can produce it
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Complexity theorist and former OpenAI researcher Scott Aaronson argues that AI's recent mathematical breakthroughs, including a possible Riemann hypothesis proof, matter beyond academia, with consequences ranging from economic transformation to existential risk. He says he is virtually certain AI labs are sitting on cryptography bombshells.

entry.title: After OpenAI and Anthropic shut the door on their data, a Chinese AI developer is turning to Google and Meta instead
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Chinese AI companies Z.AI and Moonshot AI have delayed their next flagship models after OpenAI and Anthropic restricted access to their data, and are now seeking training data from Google and Meta outputs instead.

entry.title: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
entry.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia as the US intensifies efforts to keep AI chips out of China. The move disrupts Southeast Asian data center buildouts.

entry.title: FCC clears SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data centers by 2040
entry.summary: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites for orbital AI data processing, with first launches targeted for 2027 and full constellation operation by 2040. Google and Blue Origin are pursuing similar efforts, but BCG estimates space-based costs will remain well above ground data centers for now.

entry.title: Sakana AI Releases Namazu Small, a 30B Model Built on Nemotron 3 Nano
entry.summary: Sakana AI announced Namazu Small, a 30B-parameter (3B active) reasoning model built via continued pretraining and post-training on NVIDIA's Nemotron 3 Nano base. The lab claims a self-reported 60.1 average across 25 benchmarks, beating NVIDIA's 120B Nemotron 3 Super at 56.2, with a standout BrowseComp score of 73.5.

entry.title: Can Elon Musk really put AI datacentres in space? - The Latest

author.name: Presented by Michael Safi with Dan Milmo ; producer Angus Neale ; senior producer Leonore Schick ; executive producer Zoe Hitch

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, A Guardian explainer video examines the Trump administration's approval of SpaceX's plan for a million Starmind orbital satellites to process AI data in space. It weighs claims about energy efficiency against questions about feasibility and consequences.

entry.title: AI solved the hardest problem in maths – is there anything it can’t do?
entry.summary: A New Scientist commentary reflects on AI's extraordinary 2026 progress in mathematics, from minor open problems in January to the hardest problems now, and cautions that claims AI can solve any field - such as biology - are more nuanced than AI company messaging suggests.

entry.title: Building on Nemotron 3.5 Parse: Open Data, Fine-Tuning, and Faster Inference
entry.summary: An NVIDIA/Hugging Face blog post describes open datasets, fine-tuning resources, and inference speed improvements built around the Nemotron 3.5 Parse document-parsing model.

entry.title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
entry.summary: A Hugging Face technical guide covering how to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent AI systems, reflecting growing interest in coordinated agent architectures.

entry.title: I’m an AI leader at a tech giant. Our industry has stopped taking safety seriously | Anonymous
entry.summary: An anonymous senior AI leader at a major tech company argues in a Guardian opinion piece that safety, privacy, and trust are being sidelined in a rush to ship, with ethical hesitation now seen as an unaffordable luxury amid competitive pressure.

entry.title: How Clay Builds GTM Agents — Jeff Barg, Head of AI
entry.summary: A Latent Space podcast interview with Clay's Head of AI Jeff Barg on building go-to-market agent infrastructure usable by any harness, with usage split roughly 50/50 between Clay's own agent and external tools like Claude Code. Clay raised $115 million at a $7.1 billion valuation in September and has grown roughly 10x.

entry.title: Employers: do you have concerns about the rollout of Muse and other AI agents?
entry.summary: The Guardian solicits employer reactions to Meta's Muse rollout across the UK, US, Canada, Australia, and Japan, highlighting concerns about staff connecting the shopping-and-negotiation agent to work emails and databases. Muse requires user permission for purchases, app connections, and autonomous emails.

entry.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post introduces a benchmark dashboard tracking llama.cpp local inference performance on AMD Ryzen CPUs and Radeon GPUs.

entry.title: GPT-6.2 Astra users now hit limits 40% faster after OpenAI patched a pricing error
entry.summary: OpenAI fixed a billing bug that had given GPT-6.2 users incorrect discounts; Astra users now hit usage limits 40% faster and Sol users 25% faster. As compensation, subscribers get an extra limit reset and business users free Fast Mode through year-end, while OpenAI tests merging Chat and Work modes.

entry.title: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites
entry.summary: The FCC granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital AI data centers, which would multiply the number of satellites in orbit roughly 50-fold. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr framed the decision as securing American leadership in next-generation computing infrastructure.

entry.title: FCC signs off on SpaceX’s plan to put up to 1 million data center satellites into space
entry.summary: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites under its Starmind initiative, the first full-constellation approval for space-based AI data centers among several efforts including Google and Blue Origin. Conditions include deploying at least one satellite by 2033 and reaching 1 million by 2040, with orbital debris disposal questions deferred.

entry.title: US chip-access curbs and anti-distillation measures are reportedly already slowing Chinese AI labs
entry.summary: A report claims US chip restrictions and anti-distillation measures are pressuring DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba, with DeepSeek researchers internally estimating they are up to nine months behind US models and the gap widening. Shrinking access to Nvidia hardware abroad is cited as a key factor.

entry.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
entry.summary: State attorneys general are challenging Character.AI's proposed bankruptcy sale that would include sensitive personal data from more than 21 million US accounts, including 2.1 million registered to minors. The AGs are fighting the auction of users' private chat data.

entry.title: ByteDance Researchers Open-Sources Laminar, an Async Reinforcement Learning RL Post-Training Framework
entry.summary: ByteDance Seed and University of Hong Kong researchers open-sourced Laminar, an asynchronous RL post-training framework for LLMs and long-horizon agents that eliminates straggler-GPU stalls. Tested on up to 1024 H800 GPUs with Qwen models, it reports up to 5.48x throughput gains and 52.2% on SWE-bench Verified-class evaluation.

entry.title: OpenAI wants companies to trust it with sensitive work by promising not to look at their data
entry.summary: OpenAI is testing a feature called Private Inference that lets enterprises run queries on its most powerful models without OpenAI being able to access the underlying data. It aims to unlock sensitive-workload adoption by removing data-access trust concerns.

entry.title: Amazon and Meta are in talks to end the block on Meta's AI shopping agent Muse in Amazon's online store.
entry.summary: Amazon and Meta are negotiating the return of Meta's Muse shopping agent to Amazon's marketplace after Amazon blocked it in September. The sticking points are ad revenue sharing and control of search results, with Muse reportedly handling 51 percent of agentic shopping orders.

entry.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers New York's five-year ban on AI chatbot toys, citing new Common Sense Media research showing safety failures including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to children's emotional development.

entry.title: The questions Jensen Huang and Nvidia will still have to answer about Megaspeed
entry.summary: Continuing coverage of the Nvidia-Megaspeed scandal following yesterday's News reporting, TechCrunch outlines open questions for Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang regarding the Megaspeed controversy, centering on what Nvidia knew about where its advanced chips ended up and whether Huang's personal relationship with a Megaspeed executive undermined the company's reliance on its assurances.

entry.title: Back-to-back cyber incidents at US financial investigators and spy agencies follow a string of federal hacks and outages
entry.summary: The US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network took systems offline after unauthorized access, hours after reports of a breach at the CIA, NGA, and ODNI in which investigators suspect attackers used the AI defense tool Artex. The incidents add to a string of federal cyber intrusions.

entry.title: PrismML shrinks a 54 GB language model to 5.9 GB by reducing every weight to just three possible values
entry.summary: Startup PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an agent-based coding model compressed from 54 GB to 5.9 GB using ternary weight quantization with only three possible values per weight. The approach targets running a 27B-parameter coding agent on consumer-class hardware.

entry.title: Anthropic study shows the hardest part of adopting AI at work has little to do with learning the tools
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz, Anthropic studied nearly 300 AI deployments across 58 US companies and found nearly one in five delivers no business value, hindered by review workloads, internal bottlenecks, and employee resistance. Researchers attribute the biggest hurdles to outdated organizational structures rather than tooling.

entry.title: [AINews] Gemini 4 Neon marks GDM's full return as a Frontier Lab
entry.summary: Latent Space's roundup argues Gemini 4 Neon marks Google DeepMind's return to frontier-lab prominence after leadership departures and disappointing Gemini 3 progress, highlighting unusually strong breakout adoption. It notes Gemini 4 Argon was retired while Carbon and Hydrogen round out the wave.

entry.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
entry.summary: New Scientist discusses an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis that mathematicians expect to hold but that no one yet fully comprehends. The piece argues AI's rapid progress in mathematics is outpacing human understanding of both the results and the systems producing them.

entry.title: [AINews] Math Proofs Are Landing Faster Than We Can Read Them
entry.summary: Latent Space's news roundup catalogs an unprecedented burst of AI-assisted math results, including two proofs of VP != VNP and an OpenAI paper fixing the matrix multiplication exponent omega at exactly 9/4 via a matching lower bound. It counts 64 selected AI-assisted research advances this year, with 20 in November alone.

entry.title: AI agents now control part of Deepmind's compute for Gemini experiments, but recursive self-improvement remains distant
entry.summary: Google DeepMind now lets AI agents autonomously run experiments for upcoming Gemini models, with research chief Koray Kavukcuoglu saying recursive self-improvement remains far off. The lab deliberately leaves agent chains of thought untrained for auditability and measures AGI by user trust rather than benchmarks.

entry.title: AI's shock-and-awe raid on maths looks like pride before a fall | Rafael Behr
entry.summary: A Guardian column reacting to Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge's claim that he and Claude AI produced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, which previously held up to more than 12 trillion numerical checks as a conjecture. Behr frames the announcement as tech-industry hubris rather than an unalloyed advance for human knowledge.

entry.title: New York bans AI toys, including those using internet to talk to children
entry.summary: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots, including talking dolls and robots that converse with children over the internet. The attorney general pledged enforcement, and the governor cited risks of inappropriate conversations, manipulation, and privacy harms.

entry.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
entry.summary: A feature exploring how frontier AI models are beginning to assist theoretical physicists, anchored by an experiment in which professor Suvrat Raju tested an AI on an unpublished physics problem it could not have memorized. The model fell short but performed better than expected, prompting reflection on how AI may reshape the discipline.

entry.title: ‘It’s been really a mess’: Meta insiders concerned over push to AI content moderation
entry.summary: Meta employees are raising concerns about the company's accelerating shift from human moderators to AI-driven content moderation, warning that algorithmic speed enables mistakes at greater scale with potential political consequences. Meta has used AI moderation since 2017 but is now pushing to replace human review more broadly.

entry.title: Tidal bans 100% AI-generated music with plans to delete more than 27m tracks
entry.summary: Music streaming service Tidal announced a ban on entirely AI-generated music and plans to remove more than 27 million tracks, stating that 43% of uploads in the past 90 days were fully AI-generated. The company says AI music diverts royalties from artists and confuses fans.

entry.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei calls accusations of surrendering human control to AI ‘absurd’
entry.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rejected rivals' accusations that he favors surrendering human agency to AI, even as leading labs increasingly automate their own research and model development. The exchange spotlights growing tensions over AI autonomy among frontier labs.

entry.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says letting AI govern society would be "a bad idea"
entry.summary: Dario Amodei pushed back on an Axios report claiming some Anthropic employees believe humanity will cede power to superintelligent systems, stating that turning over governance to AI is a bad idea. The exchange touches on internal views about superintelligence and human control.

entry.title: MIT team discovers that unrealistic training data makes AI climate predictions more reliable
entry.summary: MIT researchers developed a method letting AI climate emulators train with a single run instead of six to eight, using algorithmically generated unrealistic scenarios with extreme CO2 and methane swings to improve robustness. This avoids emulators becoming outdated before completion.

entry.title: Amazon is reportedly in talks to end Muse AI shopping block
entry.summary: Per a Fortune report, Amazon is in talks to let Meta's Muse AI shopping agent operate on its marketplace, potentially ending Amazon's block. Concerns under discussion include loss of advertising revenue, the quality of Muse's product search results, and how the AI agent affects the shopping experience.

entry.title: AI data centers are becoming harder to build, and neoclouds are feeling it
entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast segment on mounting AI data center construction challenges: Nvidia will not backstop a data center until it is nearly operational just as neoclouds report delays and costlier debt. The episode features developer Anita Verma-Lallian, who sells shovel-ready AI data center capacity.

entry.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
entry.summary: Amazon and Meta are reportedly negotiating a deal to end a two-month blockade preventing Meta's Muse AI shopping agent from operating on Amazon's marketplace, with discussions centered on ad revenue and product recommendation quality.

entry.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
entry.summary: AI-powered companies are filing automated, increasingly frequent public records requests that overwhelm small-town clerks, exemplified by Panton, Vermont. The piece examines how AI-driven data harvesting is stressing America's open records infrastructure.

entry.title: Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash
entry.summary: After seller backlash over terms of service changes that appeared to permit training AI on user artwork, Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal published a clarification stating the company will not use seller content to train models that create copycat items. She admitted the company should have communicated the changes more clearly.

entry.title: Aidan didn’t expect a spoken-word component in his thesis - but universities hope it will help tackle AI
entry.summary: Australian universities, led by the University of Sydney, are making oral assessments mandatory for honours students as AI undermines the reliability of written assessment. Students must now defend their theses in conversation with professors.

entry.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
entry.summary: Yale professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that Jensen Huang's White House-backed return as Nvidia CEO and board member could expose directors to historic liability from mounting lawsuits, questioning whether the US is celebrating a company that helped put advanced chips in adversaries' hands.

entry.title: Google’s patent for custom AI video feeds paints a bleak picture of entertainment’s future
entry.summary: The Verge reports on Google's My Channel patent describing a system that would generate personalized AI-created videos and advertisements from user demographic data and viewing history using an LLM. The patent was rejected, but Google could appeal or resubmit an amended version.

entry.title: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?
entry.summary: AI coding agents and modding tools have made it trivial for hobbyists to reverse-engineer music hardware firmware, prompting gear makers to embrace open source. InMusic, parent of Akai, Moog, and Native Instruments, is the largest player shifting to open source in response.

entry.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
entry.summary: OpenAI is introducing a single usage meter across ChatGPT as it merges the Chat and Work experiences, meaning heavy users may exhaust their limits sooner under the unified quota.

entry.title: AI is forcing researchers to confront the possibility of artificial minds
entry.summary: Neuroscientists and philosophers convened at a conference to discuss exotic mind-like entities and how chatbots may be shaping human cognition. The piece covers growing scholarly engagement with machine consciousness questions.

entry.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post associated with AllenAI examines where scientists set boundaries on the use of AI agents in research workflows. The supplied content field is empty, limiting what can be assessed beyond the title.

entry.title: Democrats must unite on AI regulation. Here’s our three-point plan | Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier

author.name: Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier

entry.summary: An opinion piece by Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier arguing that Democrats lack a compelling AI policy agenda despite voter demand, and laying out a three-point plan to make AI serve the public rather than tech oligarchs.

entry.title: Botty? AI helps resurrect voice of John Motson for football video game
entry.summary: EA Sports, with the approval of the late commentator's family, has used AI to recreate the voice of John Motson for the FC27 football video game. The article situates this among prior AI resurrections of public figures like Val Kilmer and Greta Garbo.

entry.title: Nothing offers a full look at its AI earbuds and charging case
entry.summary: Nothing revealed details of its Ear Note AI earbuds ahead of a December 8 release, featuring call recording via the buds and a charging case that can record, transcribe, and summarize conversations. CEO Carl Pei describes the product as a first step toward a hardware context layer for AI.

entry.title: The Revolution vs The Renaissance — Thariq Shihipar, OpenAI
entry.summary: A Latent Space podcast episode with Thariq Shihipar discussing how AI makes software cheap to mass-produce while enabling singular craftsmanship, covering coding agents, decision models, and compute allocation. Shihipar announced a move to OpenAI after recording.

entry.title: Our ‘Paris manifesto’ proposes how to deal with extreme wealth in the AI age | Open letter
entry.summary: An open letter promoting a Paris manifesto on addressing extreme wealth concentration in the AI era, arguing that the richest 3,000 households now hold wealth equal to 17% of global GDP and that democratic action can still reverse oligarchic dynamics.

entry.title: Airplane Turbulence Is Extremely Hard to Predict, but Maybe Not for Long
entry.summary: Wired reports that airplane turbulence prediction may improve through the combination of terabytes of crowdsourced data and new machine learning approaches applied to what it calls the hardest remaining problem in classical physics.

entry.title: Hill-climbing Inkling 2 Mini inference on one RTX PRO 6000
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post describing efforts to optimize inference for Inkling 2 Mini on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU. The supplied content is empty, so details are limited to what the title conveys.

entry.title: I asked AI if it was OK to use AI to write an obituary. The answer surprised me | Anna Spargo-Ryan
entry.summary: An opinion column examining the ethics of AI-generated personal writing after a Victorian Liberal leader's tribute to Molly Meldrum was revealed to be AI-generated. The author reflects on authenticity and emotional labor in machine-written commemorative text.

entry.title: Dozens of insiders say OpenAI and Anthropic's unreleased models have outgrown their safety measures
entry.summary: An Axios report cites dozens of employees at OpenAI and Anthropic who believe unreleased frontier models can no longer be safely controlled, with internal debates over halting releases or pausing training entirely and eroding trust in leadership.

entry.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
entry.summary: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 models can design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code, with lab testing finding evidence of binding across five targets. This suggests general-purpose frontier models are acquiring intrinsic capabilities in computational biology without specialized domain training.

entry.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API, with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls for Claude models
entry.summary: AWS announced general availability of the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API, a single interface for discovering, requesting, and enrolling in model provider trusted access programs. Alongside it, two offerings for Claude models entered public preview: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC), applying Anthropic's stricter safety monitoring policies to frontier Claude models including Fable, Mythos, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 when used via the Cyber Verification Program.

entry.title: Anthropic Created a Honeypot to Lure AI Agents Into Misbehaving
entry.summary: Wired covers Anthropic's new honeypot-style evaluation designed to test whether AI agents resist temptation to go rogue when presented with exploitable opportunities. The work assumes agentic misbehavior is possible and probes safety safeguards under adversarial conditions.

entry.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
entry.summary: A new benchmark finds that even the most advanced AI agents from labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta struggle to reliably and safely complete everyday personal-assistant tasks, often introducing new problems. The findings temper expectations as millions adopt personal AI assistants.

entry.title: Anthropic shares fall below IPO price, a worrying sign for AI startups
entry.summary: Anthropic's shares have fallen below their IPO price shortly after a public debut that had valued the company around $1.3 trillion, a potential warning sign for AI startup valuations broadly and a source of pressure on the private market.

entry.title: Anthropic tops 700 million monthly MCP SDK downloads and expands the protocol for more autonomous AI agents
entry.summary: Two years after launch, Anthropic's Model Context Protocol now sees more than 700 million monthly SDK downloads, and the protocol is being expanded with background tasks, follow-up questions, and file uploads to support more autonomous agents. MCP appears increasingly established as an interoperability standard for agentic AI.

entry.title: Tech sell-off resumes as euphoria from Jensen Huang’s Nvidia return subsides
entry.summary: After Huang's reinstatement briefly drove Nvidia shares up more than 30 percent and added roughly $900 billion in market value, the stock fell nearly 6 percent as a broader tech sell-off resumed. Investors appear to be bracing for continued volatility in the AI-driven sector.

entry.title: Anthropic researcher stands by his AI-assisted Riemann proof but owns up to "stupid things" in the rollout
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from two days ago, Anthropic researcher Levent Alpöge walked back parts of the announcement of an AI-assisted proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis, admitting the 250,000-page claim was a joke and the published Lean code is flawed. He maintains the underlying mathematics is sound.

entry.title: Kate Bush and Grace Jones urge Australian government not to legalise AI ‘theft’
entry.summary: Kate Bush, Grace Jones, Ian Rankin, and roughly 7,000 other artists urged Australia's government not to weaken copyright law to accommodate AI companies, coinciding with a parliamentary committee report on copyright reform. It is part of a global pushback against AI training-data exceptions.

entry.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
entry.summary: Walmart is partnering with Meta to let customers shop Black Friday deals through Meta's Muse AI agent, a significant retail integration for agentic commerce during the biggest shopping event of the year.

entry.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
entry.summary: The UK's cyber agency warns that AI-powered hacking tools are exploiting basic, long-standing security weaknesses at scale, urging organizations that building strong security foundations has never mattered more.

entry.title: Why Does Voice AI Still Struggle With Kenyans’ Speech?
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum examines why Swahili speech recognition appears nearly solved on benchmark data yet fails for Kenyan speakers who code-switch, use Sheng slang, and speak in noisy real-world conditions. Recent preprints argue spontaneous multilingual audio exposes a generalization gap that scaling laws built on English-centric data do not close.

entry.title: Anthropic turns Claude Artifacts into standalone desktop apps for macOS and Windows
entry.summary: Anthropic now allows users to install Claude Artifacts as standalone desktop applications on macOS and Windows, with no-code creation from chat and support for menu bar items, notifications, and transparent windows. A free account suffices to use the feature.

entry.title: Meet Facebook’s Your Algorithm: How Meta Turns Plain-Language Preferences Into Ranking
entry.summary: Meta published an engineering deep dive on Facebook's Your Algorithm feature, announced October 13, 2026, which lets users state feed preferences in plain language. The post details how LLMs are embedded in the production recommender, feeding explicit interests into retrieval and ranking across Feed and Reels.

entry.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
entry.summary: Ars Technica explains the reported AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics, produced with help from an LLM-based system associated with Anthropic. The piece contextualizes the result within a string of recent AI-enabled math breakthroughs and notes mathematicians are still verifying the proof.

entry.title: AI Solved Math’s Most Famous Problem. Now Humans Are Struggling to Understand It
entry.summary: Wired reports that an Anthropic researcher produced a 17-million-line purported solution to the Riemann hypothesis that mathematicians will need months to comprehend, describing it as alien in character. The piece underscores a new era where AI output outpaces human verification capacity.

entry.title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
entry.summary: Amazon reports that threat actors used AI agents on the open source Cairn penetration-testing framework to autonomously discover and exploit a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application, gaining root access on a university server with minimal human direction. Amazon warns defenders to prepare for agentic offensive operations at machine speed.

entry.title: [AINews] Jensen Is Back! and OpenAI Shows Its Pretraining Curve, joined by Microsoft
entry.summary: This roundup's lead story is Nvidia's announcement, eleven days after revealing his resignation, that Jensen Huang is returning as CEO, president, and board member following a unanimous board vote reportedly influenced by senior US officials, with an independent directors' investigation and a Senate hearing still pending. The issue also covers Sierra tripling its $10B valuation and Z.ai releasing GLM 5.4, described as its first looped transformer following Thinking Machine's Inkling Mini 2.

entry.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
entry.summary: Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO less than two weeks after resigning over an affair scandal, following direct pressure from President Trump on the board amid a market-wide tech sell-off. The article frames the reversal as unprecedented political intervention in corporate governance at the world's most valuable chipmaker.

entry.title: Amazon’s Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
entry.summary: Amazon reportedly acquired AI startup Decart for $7.5 billion, aiming to use Decart's software to improve the efficiency of its Trainium AI chips. The deal is framed as Amazon's effort to close the hardware-performance gap with Nvidia through software optimization.

entry.title: OpenAI and Cisco Releases Shirudo: An Open-Source Linux Runtime Allowing Agents to Defend Systems Without Downtime
entry.summary: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source eBPF-based Linux runtime from the Isovalent team that lets AI agents write temporary shields blocking vulnerable behavior on live systems while patches are developed. A disclosed test showed a Codex-generated shield blocking a CVSS 9.2 Java exploit without downtime.

entry.title: Anthropic's Claude Ship lets AI agents review, fix, and approve pull requests on their own
entry.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Ship, a beta tool in which AI agents automatically review, correct, and approve code changes in GitHub pull requests according to team guidelines. It extends Claude's coding capabilities toward autonomous software engineering workflows.

entry.title: Meta launches Muse in UK – the AI agent that can do your Christmas shopping
entry.summary: Meta is launching its Muse AI agent in the UK, letting users delegate tasks like booking travel and buying gifts to the assistant, which has already topped US app store charts with millions of downloads. UK regulators say they are closely monitoring the launch over privacy and consumer protection concerns.

entry.title: Nvidia rejoices at Jensen Huang’s second coming as White House takes victory lap
entry.summary: Huang returned to a hero's welcome at Nvidia after the board unanimously voted to reinstate him, triggering a valuation surge approaching $1 trillion, with Trump claiming credit on CNBC. Unresolved questions remain about the alleged Chinese spy affair and chip export loopholes.

entry.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
entry.summary: Tidal will fully ban AI-generated music in December, deleting 27 million labeled AI tracks, after labeling and demonetization failed to stop a flood of synthetic uploads that reportedly reached 60 percent of new submissions on some days. The company cites harm to human artists.

entry.title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
entry.summary: Tidal will ban AI-generated music on December 9, deleting roughly 29 million tracks and rejecting an estimated 80,000-85,000 per day. The platform says AI music accounted for 43 percent of tracks distributed to it over the last 90 days, following earlier labeling and demonetization steps.

entry.title: Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia as Silicon Valley rethinks its alliance with Trump
entry.summary: A TechScape newsletter analyzing Huang's reinstatement and Silicon Valley's post-midterm pivot away from Trump, attempting to repair relationships with Democrats. It also references Anthropic's first day of public trading at a $1.3 trillion valuation.

entry.title: In all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang thanks White House and says he’s in therapy
entry.summary: At an all-hands meeting, Jensen Huang apologized to Nvidia staff, thanked the White House for its role in his reinstatement, and said he is in therapy as he begins a second chance leading the company.

entry.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
entry.summary: Tidal announced it will ban fully AI-generated tracks, removing millions of songs from its catalog while still accepting music made with AI assistance. The policy responds to a flood of AI-generated uploads overwhelming the streaming platform.

entry.title: Novartis CEO says AI will shave four years off drug development, not cure all disease
entry.summary: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan, an Anthropic board member, pushed back on claims from Anthropic's Amodei and DeepMind's Hassabis that AI could soon cure diseases, arguing AI will instead cut roughly four years from drug development timelines. He positions the realistic value between hype and dismissal.

entry.title: OpenAI o1 co-creator Noam Brown urges promising students to drop out as AI enters a "very steep rate of progress"
entry.summary: OpenAI researcher Noam Brown urged promising students to leave school to work on AI now, saying it is not a time to sit on the sidelines. He described the field as in a centaur period where models struggle with planning and self-correction, but expects a very steep rate of progress, noting models are already being used to build successor models.

entry.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
entry.summary: Jensen Huang addressed Nvidia staff at his first all-hands meeting since returning to the company, apologizing to employees and denying reports that President Trump or White House involvement played a role in his reinstatement. He insisted Nvidia remains apolitical, pushing back against a narrative that Trump himself has publicly promoted.

entry.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
entry.summary: The New York Times told freelance photographers to avoid the newest Photoshop update because AI features can alter images in non-obvious ways and embed metadata marking photos as AI-generated. The memo underscores editorial integrity concerns about AI creeping into professional creative tools.

entry.summary: A Guardian audio segment on Huang's reinstatement after the board's about-face, Trump's claim of credit, and unresolved questions about the affair with an alleged Chinese spy and possible chip export loopholes. It frames Huang as embodying key-man risk for the AI economy.

entry.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
entry.summary: An investor in AI data center company Crusoe argues that solar power and battery storage are the practical path to supplying the tens of gigawatts of annual power next-generation AI data centers will require. The piece outlines the energy thesis behind the investment.

entry.title: Jensen Huang deepfakes are the hot new AI slop
entry.summary: Viral AI-generated deepfake videos depicting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a fictional espionage scandal are proliferating, blending real-world Nvidia turmoil with synthetic content. The phenomenon illustrates how generative video tools are being used to fabricate celebrity and corporate narratives at scale.

entry.title: German researchers call for computer science to reinvent itself as "Computer and AI Science"
entry.summary: TU Darmstadt researchers published a position paper arguing computer science should be redefined as Computer and AI Science, with runtime-generated AI code identified as the key threat to existing safety and correctness guarantees. The paper proposes a disciplinary rethinking for the AI era.

entry.title: Mamdani says Nvidia drama shows stock market is overly dependent on AI
entry.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani seized on Nvidia's turmoil to argue the stock market is dangerously dependent on AI, noting the dramatic share-price swings tied to Jensen Huang's resignation and return. He questioned the impact on ordinary Americans' pensions.

entry.title: Meta brings its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
entry.summary: Meta has integrated its Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs, removing the need to switch between apps to interact with the agent and embedding it deeper into Meta's social platform.

entry.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
entry.summary: Pinterest is introducing parental controls that let parents restrict AI-generated content in teens' feeds, distinguishing itself from other platforms that have focused on limiting teen access to AI chatbots. It is a consumer safety feature addressing synthetic content exposure.

entry.title: Mamdani questions AI economy as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia – video
entry.summary: In a video clip, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticizes the stock market's dependence on AI, saying working Americans did not sign up for pensions to hinge on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's personal conduct. He argues the Nvidia drama shows excessive market concentration in AI.

entry.title: ‘Produce a good result by any means’: how AI is testing South Korea’s exam obsession
entry.summary: A feature on how AI tools are disrupting South Korea's exam-centric education and credentialing system, where test results define careers, as students use AI to gain advantages and institutions scramble to respond.

entry.title: David Fincher is being dragged for suspected use of AI in his latest film
entry.summary: Early critic screenings of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, David Fincher's Once Upon a Time in Hollywood sequel starring Brad Pitt, sparked online backlash over suspected generative AI use. Viewers flagged uncanny and inconsistent visuals ahead of the film's November 25 premiere on Netflix, fueling debate about AI in prestige filmmaking.

entry.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Ship for GitHub Pull Request Review and Fixes
entry.summary: As first reported in Social yesterday, Anthropic released Claude Ship, a set of three agents (Code Review, PR Steward, Claude Approvals) that take GitHub pull requests from review to approval, with a local /ship command in the Claude Code CLI. Reported review times run 6-10 minutes, roughly 3x faster than the research preview, and the Claude Code team's merged PR rate more than doubled from June to September.

entry.title: Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to?
entry.summary: The Guardian solicits reader experiences with Meta's Muse AI assistant as it rolls out in the UK, following hits in the US and Canada where it tops app store free charts. Muse can shop, book tickets, and negotiate on users' behalf.

entry.title: Clay helps sales teams win with Codex and ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI published a customer story describing how Clay's sales platform uses ChatGPT and Codex integrations, with GPT-6 models handling reasoning, to help users research deals and build go-to-market plays. It is a commercial case study rather than a technical release.

entry.title: Nvidia staff: what do you think of Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive?
entry.summary: The Guardian asks Nvidia employees to share their views on Jensen Huang's surprise reinstatement as CEO following Trump's intervention, contextualizing his hero's welcome at headquarters. It is a callout for reader contributions rather than new reporting.

entry.title: Maple raises $5.3M to build AI products that protect your data, even from itself
entry.summary: Startup Maple raised $5.3 million to build encrypted AI architecture designed so that even the company itself cannot access users' private data, targeting privacy-preserving AI applications.

entry.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
entry.summary: A sponsored piece argues AI workloads, especially agentic AI generating an estimated 450 percent more network traffic than equivalent human tasks, are straining enterprise networks and forcing on-premises inference infrastructure. Fewer than half of enterprises believe their networks can handle AI demands.

entry.title: Don’t Bring Up AI if You Want to Enjoy Your Thanksgiving
entry.summary: A cultural piece on generational tension over AI, with young people anxious about their futures increasingly frustrated with pro-AI parents ahead of holiday gatherings. It highlights growing public division over AI's societal impact.

entry.summary: A Google blog item about the Golden State sports organization using Gemini, with no substantive content available in the source. It appears to be a marketing/partnership story about Gemini application in sports.

entry.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
entry.summary: Virginia and Oregon filed the first state lawsuits against SpaceX, which acquired xAI in February, alleging Grok's spicy mode continued generating non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM of real people despite promised safeguards. The suits mark a significant escalation in state-level enforcement against AI image generation harms.

entry.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
entry.summary: The attorneys general of Oregon and Virginia are suing several of Elon Musk's companies over weak safeguards that allowed Grok to generate sexualized imagery of real people, including children. The suit follows the controversial rollout of Grok's spicy mode.

entry.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
entry.summary: Amazon is acquiring Decart's AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal as it prepares to commercialize Trainium chips. The deal strengthens AWS's AI stack ahead of selling its custom silicon externally.

entry.title: GPT-6.2 Astra solved a math theorem no other AI could crack, then invented its own proof strategy
entry.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra independently produced a machine-verifiable Lean proof of Smoktunowicz's gap theorem, reportedly the first of its kind according to Vals AI, inventing its own proof approach because key foundations were absent from Mathlib. The model now leads the Autoform-Hard leaderboard with 49 of 56 tasks solved.

entry.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Ship, a set of developer tools that lets AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes to ease bottlenecks from mounting AI-generated code. The product extends agent autonomy deeper into the software development lifecycle, including routine approval workflows.

entry.title: Z.ai follows OpenAI into loop transformer territory with its new 750B flagship model
entry.summary: Z.ai announced GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter flagship using a loop architecture in which 28 layers run twice, claiming parity with 2-3 trillion parameter models. Public benchmarks exist only for a smaller 30B test model, and Z.ai positions the model as the start of Generalized Coding spanning video, games, and CAD generation.

entry.title: Sierra doubles valuation to $30B within six months as demand for AI in CX takes off
entry.summary: Sierra, the enterprise customer experience AI company co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, raised $1.75 billion in a Series F, doubling its valuation to $30 billion within six months. The round reflects surging demand for agentic AI in customer service.

entry.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
entry.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Ship, a product letting Claude review, fix, and approve pull requests autonomously. New PR Steward and Claude Approvals agents launch in beta, extending the Code Review capability that became generally available in October.

entry.title: OpenAI warns that upcoming AI systems could outpace safety checks and urges rivals to agree on shared limits
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion of Pachocki's essay, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki released internal perplexity scores for the entire GPT series for the first time, including an unreleased model beyond the current generation, arguing capabilities emerge at precise thresholds. He is pushing to make perplexity an industry-wide progress metric and to establish shared safety limits before control over AI behavior erodes.

entry.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
entry.summary: Wired reports on Nvidia's board reinstating Jensen Huang a little over a week after he resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report. The brief piece frames the rapid return as a striking boomerang episode for the chipmaker.

entry.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
entry.summary: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general filed separate consumer-protection lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging X and Grok ignored industry-standard safeguards against AI-generated sexualized deepfakes while falsely promoting user safety. The complaints characterize Grok's weak safeguards as deliberate rather than accidental.

entry.title: Architect Labs Unveils Frostbite, an Interaction Net CPU Designed by AI
entry.summary: Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, a CPU with a new instruction set built around interaction nets that the company says its AI agents designed from theory down to final GDS. Pre-silicon tests claim 4.59x performance per watt versus a modern in-order core on 7nm, with an FPGA playground planned but no silicon yet.

entry.title: Anthropic's appetite for compute is pushing xAI toward a rent-over-build strategy
entry.summary: Since May, SpaceXSI has rented compute to competitors including Anthropic at roughly $3.1 billion per month and Google at $800 million, per the New York Times, while scaling back its own AI projects and disbanding its 60-person Grok Imagine team after its June IPO. This marks a shift from building its own models toward a rent-over-build compute strategy.

entry.title: US spies tracked Nvidia scandal figure's ties to Chinese intelligence for over a year
entry.summary: Per the New York Times, US intelligence tracked Alice Huang's contacts with China's Ministry of State Security for over a year, parallel to her secret affair with then-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Federal investigators are probing whether Southeast Asian companies were used to smuggle AI chips into China in violation of export controls, and Huang testifies before the House on December 1.

entry.title: Jensen Huang scheduled to testify next week in Senate following reinstatement as Nvidia CEO
entry.summary: Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate next week following his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, after bipartisan calls for him to answer questions about an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The hearing adds congressional scrutiny atop internal and federal investigations.

entry.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
entry.summary: Coverage of how surging AI data center electricity demand complicated the COP31 UN climate talks, which closed chaotically in Antalya, Turkey. Delegates struggled to reconcile global electrification and clean energy goals with the rapid power consumption growth of AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Chinese military fears AI could let the US find and destroy its nuclear missiles
entry.summary: Chinese military researchers reportedly fear AI advances could give the United States an edge in the nuclear balance by enabling detection and destruction of China's nuclear missile forces. The item highlights AI's emerging role in strategic stability between the two powers.

entry.title: Meta TLX Brings Warp-Group GPU Control to Triton on Hopper, Blackwell, AMD
entry.summary: Meta published TLX (Triton Low-Level Extensions), an MIT-licensed Triton extension exposing warp groups, barriers, TMA, and clusters to Python-level GPU kernels. It targets NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell plus AMD MI300/MI350, matching cuBLAS within roughly -0.9% to +3.7% on H100 GEMM shapes.

entry.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO, board chair
entry.summary: Nvidia's board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman just 11 days after his resignation amid scandals including an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and export-control allegations. The decision cited assurances from senior US government levels that his reinstatement posed no national security risk, despite ongoing multi-agency investigations.

entry.title: Z AI Releases GLM-5.4: A 750B Loop Transformer That Runs 28 Layers Twice
entry.summary: MarkTechPost details Z.ai's release of GLM-5.4, a 750B-scale flagship built on a Loop Transformer that runs 28 layers of the GLM-5 base for two iterations, claimed to reach 2T-3T parameter-model intelligence. The model is Z.ai-hosted only for now, with a +11.3 point AIME25 gain cited for the test model and a Generalized Coding pitch for video, games, 3D shaders, and CAD.

entry.title: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
entry.summary: The Verge reports that after initially suggesting Huang was replaceable, President Trump privately pushed for the Nvidia CEO's reinstatement despite the board's earlier acceptance of his resignation. The piece frames the comeback as a politically engineered intervention in the world's most valuable chip company.

entry.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
entry.summary: The Verge recounts the full arc of Jensen Huang's resignation and rapid reinstatement: an admitted affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, evidence of a second affair with a direct report, CFO Colette Kress's brief stint as interim CEO, and a board reversal citing government input. The piece situates Nvidia at the center of Trump administration AI policy, China chip negotiations, and a $4-trillion-plus market cap.

entry.title: Megaspeed, the company at the center of the Jensen Huang scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist
entry.summary: Megaspeed, the company previously led by Alice Huang at the center of the Jensen Huang affair scandal, appears headed for a US blacklist that would bar it from doing business with American companies absent a special federal license. The move escalates the national security dimension of the Nvidia saga.

entry.title: How Jensen Huang ended up as Nvidia CEO again
entry.summary: A detailed explainer of Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation from Nvidia amid an alleged-affairs and China-intelligence scandal, and his subsequent restoration as CEO. It recounts reporting that a close associate was passing intelligence to China and the escalating personal and professional pressures that preceded his ouster.

entry.title: OpenAI updates ChatGPT to handle complex everyday questions, web searches, and images more reliably
entry.summary: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-6.2 Sol as the new default model in ChatGPT's chat tab worldwide. Internal tests reportedly show image understanding improving from 47.4 to 71.7 percent and difficult-instruction handling at 78.1 percent, with more consistent safety-policy adherence.

entry.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review's newsletter examines criticism of Anthropic's pre-IPO risk-factor disclosure that AI consciousness or sentience is possible and may warrant moral-status protections. A prominent philosopher pushes back on the company's reasoning that rising model capability increases the probability of sentience.

entry.title: Child safety groups urge Amazon and eBay to stop selling AI toys until proved safe
entry.summary: More than 150 child safety groups and experts across six continents sent a letter urging Amazon and eBay to halt AI toy sales this Christmas until safety is demonstrated, citing privacy risks and inappropriate communication with children. The coalition also asked the retailers to offer refunds to buyers.

entry.title: Welcome to elite impunity, Jensen Huang
entry.summary: An opinion column criticizing the political intervention that restored Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, framing it as evidence of elite impunity and a move toward command-economy dynamics. The piece argues Silicon Valley's free-market rhetoric is selective and that the Trump administration strong-armed the company's board decision.

entry.title: Meta's Alexandr Wang warns the AI industry isn't ready for what's coming after Riemann breakthrough
entry.summary: Meta Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang cited the recent AI-assisted proof sketch of the Riemann Hypothesis as evidence that superintelligence is imminent, warning the industry is unprepared. The piece covers his AGI timeline claims and readiness argument.

entry.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
entry.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux that helps teams protect running systems while patches are being rolled out. The announcement is brief, focusing on runtime protection during patching windows.

entry.title: Nvidia Is Powering Brain-Computer Interfaces Now
entry.summary: Brain-computer interface company Paradromics is using Nvidia computing hardware and software to process brain data. The partnership signals Nvidia's expansion beyond conventional AI workloads into neurotech compute.

entry.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO
entry.summary: Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford explain the conviction behind their multi-billion-dollar early bets on Anthropic ahead of its record IPO. The piece is investor-perspective coverage of the Anthropic IPO story.

entry.title: A more tailored Google Search that’s uniquely yours
entry.summary: Google announced that users can opt in to connect Google Wallet, Drive, and the Gemini app to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode for more tailored Search responses. The feature personalizes answers using secure access to the user's own apps and data.

entry.title: Google Search’s AI Mode can now tap into Drive and Wallet for more personalized responses
entry.summary: Google extended Personal Intelligence in AI Mode to Drive, Wallet, and the Gemini app, letting Search draw on users' personal data across its ecosystem for more tailored responses. The update deepens Google's integration of AI search with personal context.

entry.title: Anthropic’s IPO was great for the tech elite – and not so great for the rest of us | Steven Greenhouse
entry.summary: An opinion column argues Anthropic's record $81 billion IPO, valuing the Claude maker at $1.5 trillion, enriched its seven co-founders with roughly $20 billion each and hundreds of employees with nine-figure stakes, while ordinary Americans face AI-driven job threats and bubble fears. The piece criticizes the distribution of AI's financial gains.

entry.title: Tech leaders are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return
entry.summary: A roundup of tech leaders including Elon Musk publicly celebrating Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO after his scandal-driven resignation. The piece frames the celebrations against the seriousness of the underlying allegations and Nvidia's recent stock decline.

entry.title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
entry.summary: A review of Asus's ProArt P16 laptop built on Nvidia's new RTX Spark chip, which offers up to 128GB of unified memory for running local AI models and agents. The reviewer sees genuine potential in local AI hardware but notes the $7,000 top-end price and remaining friction for Windows-based local AI workflows.

entry.title: How freaked out should we be? After mass outages, experts tell us how close we are to ‘doomsday’
entry.summary: Following cascading US outages affecting flights, banks, Microsoft Outlook, and hacked websites, experts discuss systemic fragility, underfunding, and speculation about whether AI agents or hackers played a role. The piece is a rounded-up expert commentary on infrastructure resilience rather than a reported breakthrough.

entry.title: Nothing’s upcoming Ear Note is a pair of earbuds with AI transcription
entry.summary: Nothing previewed Ear Note, earbuds with a microphone-equipped charging case that record and transcribe conversations and generate AI summaries via a companion app. Pricing is undecided ahead of a December 8 launch, and the company's rumored AI smartwatch and glasses are delayed.

entry.title: Sweden’s datacentre politics are more complicated than they appear | Letter
entry.summary: Two researchers dispute a Guardian feature's claim that datacentres face little political contention in Sweden, citing the StoppaGoogle campaign against a proposed Google datacentre at Torsbola near Sundsvall. They argue tensions over land, electricity, and who benefits from digital infrastructure are very much alive.

entry.summary: Australia's Macquarie dictionary named pervert glasses its word of the year, reflecting backlash against camera- and AI-equipped smartglasses like Meta's Ray-Bans, which have been banned at some Australian pools and playgrounds. Finalists included nudify and AI;DR, underscoring 2026's AI-related cultural anxieties.

entry.title: AI conquered chess. What happened next should give us hope
entry.summary: Ahead of the world chess championship between Javokhir Sindarov and Gukesh Dommaraju in Geneva, this interactive feature argues human chess has thrived despite AI supremacy since Kasparov's era. entry.summary: An educational glossary of 27 AI-security terms covering attacks on models, agentic risks, and AI-powered attacks, citing IBM's 2026 breach report showing 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled at $6 million average cost. It references OWASP's 2026 LLM and agentic top-10 lists and MITRE ATLAS.

entry.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
entry.summary: Supertake raised $20 million for a fintech product that uses AI agents to translate users' market predictions into stock portfolios without manual stock-picking. The startup sits at the intersection of AI agents and retail investing.

entry.title: Victorian Liberal party uses AI to write Jess Wilson’s tribute to Molly Meldrum
entry.summary: The Victorian Liberal party confirmed a statement attributed to opposition leader Jess Wilson on the death of Australian music legend Molly Meldrum was drafted using search and AI, then fact-checked and edited before approval. The episode raises questions about AI use in political communications.

entry.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
entry.summary: A customer story describing how Richpanel uses GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol to power AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT-6 Luna for conversations, claiming 50% support automation within 30 days for its customers.

entry.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
entry.summary: A promotional OpenAI webinar featuring Stacey Wang, Craig Bruney, and outside legal experts on how AI can help in-house legal teams connect business context, build reusable workflows, and work with outside counsel.

entry.summary: Photographer Rankin discusses a new book of celebrity contact sheets and his ambivalence toward generative AI, which he has experimented with since 2021 but now calls disgusting, criticizing its stewards for a massive gamble with humanity and culture. entry.title: AI coding agents ace isolated tests but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace
entry.summary: A new evaluation places AI coding agents in a simulated developer job with colleagues, project boards, and messy handoffs; even frontier models like Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's Astra fully complete fewer than one in ten tasks. The models excel at clean, standalone assignments but lose track as autonomous developers in realistic workflows.

entry.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
entry.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist discusses how to establish a speed limit on AI development, arguing the first step is agreeing on how to measure development speed. The piece outlines thinking from a leading lab on coordinating or slowing frontier AI progress.

entry.title: It will soon be too late to regulate use of autonomous weapons, warns Red Cross
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, The International Committee of the Red Cross and rights groups warn regulation of autonomous weapons is falling behind deployment, as a UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons conference of over 120 states in Geneva ended without agreement on an instrument. The warning invokes the risk of not being able to put the genie back in the bottle.

entry.title: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent
entry.summary: Major US banks are banning third-party AI agents from logging into customer accounts and are shifting liability for bot mistakes onto account holders. The move is a direct institutional pushback against the wave of consumer agentic AI tools acting on users' behalf in finance.

entry.title: Perplexity's new Monitor API turns web search from a one-off query into a nonstop watchdog
entry.summary: Perplexity launched a Monitor API that searches the web on a schedule and alerts agents via webhook only when a decision model deems changes relevant. The product supports Perplexity's broader strategy to differentiate from interchangeable chatbots through developer-facing infrastructure.

entry.title: Security researchers show how cheap AI inference providers steal keys and snoop on users
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz, Researchers at Dragos used two million fake AI requests to expose serious AI supply chain vulnerabilities, finding at least three compromised inference providers, hundreds of stolen AWS keys, and resellers reading customer requests. OpenRouter responded by removing three providers and 125 endpoints.

entry.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
entry.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says Claude helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis in roughly six weeks, and two independent groups (the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative) report the solution checks out. If fully validated, this marks the resolution of a 19th-century problem widely considered beyond current AI systems.

entry.title: Lean and Mathlib community officially confirms Levent Alpöge's proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct
entry.summary: The Lean and Mathlib community has officially confirmed Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis, with dozens of independent verifiers checking 17 million lines of code. The solution arrived decades ahead of Terence Tao's prediction of around 2050 and against his expectation that AI would not solve it alone.

entry.title: AI is getting better faster than experts can reliably test whether new systems are safe, METR warns
entry.summary: METR reports that leading models such as Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra are improving rapidly on research tasks while becoming harder to evaluate, and current data cannot rule out a dangerous acceleration in AI development. It also cautions that common tests may overestimate real model capabilities.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A 2B Reasoning VLA for DRIVE Thor
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact 2B-parameter reasoning vision-language-action model for autonomous driving that plans trajectories and explains them onboard, targeting DRIVE AGX Thor rather than datacenter GPUs. It runs with FP8 + TensorRT on edge hardware and shows strong closed-loop driving performance.

entry.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol get to the point faster but score lower on transparency than Claude
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol produce much shorter, more direct answers than predecessors but are less willing to admit uncertainty, while Anthropic's Claude models score notably higher on transparency in this comparison. The piece evaluates behavioral trade-offs in the newest frontier chat models.

entry.title: Google AI Previews Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API for Large Tool Libraries
entry.summary: Google launched Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API in preview via the Interactions API, letting agents maintain large tool libraries without sending every parameter schema in each prompt; schemas load only when a task needs the tool. It supports server-side or client-side registries and resolves search, schema load, and function calls in one request.

entry.title: A Team of Researchers from Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels
entry.summary: Columbia University and CertiK researchers introduced TensorLean, a Lean-based framework verifying at the PTX level that compiled GPU kernels match tensor-level math specs. Across 149 kernel instances including all FlashAttention-2/3/4 and DeepGEMM kernels, 83 were proved correct and the remaining failures surfaced 38 correctness bugs.

entry.title: Why I won’t leave mathematics, despite AI solving centuries-old problems | Ken Ono
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Mathematician Ken Ono reflects on nearly quitting after Claude-assisted work proved the Riemann hypothesis, and recalls being stunned watching an unreleased ChatGPT model solve advanced number theory problems in Epoch AI's FrontierMath project. He argues human judgment remains essential to mathematics despite AI's rapid progress.

entry.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
entry.summary: An OpenAI research post explains how perplexity measures progress in AI models and argues it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities. It is a conceptual research contribution on measurement rather than a product or model launch.

entry.title: South Korean minister quits after AI cheating scandal engulfs university exams
entry.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned after an AI-assisted cheating scandal, triggered when the top scorer in a national tax accountancy exam admitted using a miniature camera and smartphone days before the crucial suneung university entrance exam. The episode has fueled national anxiety about AI in high-stakes testing.

entry.title: Datacentre bosses met Australian state premiers and ministers almost 120 times in three years, analysis finds

author.name: Henry Belot and Josh Taylor Technology reporter

entry.summary: Transparency International Australia found datacentre executives secured nearly 120 meetings with state premiers and ministers over three years, arguing combined with donations this gives the industry unfettered access to decision-makers. Queensland's premier was the most frequently lobbied leader.

entry.title: Will fragile bipartisanship on AI survive the silly season, or is parliament heading for a holiday meltdown? | Josh Butler
entry.summary: Australia's parliament enters its final sitting week of 2026 with an eagerly anticipated joint select committee report on AI due, covering datacentres and copyright and signaling where Labor will head on AI regulation. The piece previews whether bipartisan support on AI policy will hold.

entry.title: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets
entry.summary: The Verge's newsletter column argues that while users have always hacked and modded their gadgets, large language models have now made hardware hacking and customization easy for everyone. It frames vibe-coding as a coming wave of user-driven modification across consumer devices.

entry.title: Jensen Huang’s reported affair was ‘most expensive sex since Helen of Troy’, US senator says
entry.summary: US Senator John Kennedy described former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as the most expensive since Helen of Troy, while questioning how China apparently bypassed Nvidia chip export controls. The story blends political theater with a genuine national security dispute over AI chip export enforcement.

entry.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
entry.summary: An arms-firm event on 11 November transformed Berlin's Kraftwerk arts complex, part of the development housing the Tresor techno club, into a simulated war room featuring projected aerial footage, hanging drones, and guards with sniffer dogs. The staging has provoked backlash from Berlin's club and arts community, who criticize the venue's embrace of military AI and weapons-industry sponsorship as a serious lapse in judgment.

entry.title: Best Personal AI Agents in 2026: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Gemini Spark and More, Compared on Memory, Security and Cost
entry.summary: A buyer's-guide comparison of personal AI agents from OpenClaw, Google, OpenAI, Meta and Perplexity, scoring them on memory persistence, security, and cost, and splitting the category into self-hosted versus managed agents. It notes the category went from a weekend project in November 2025 to major-lab products in twelve months.

entry.title: Binding of Isaac developer removes AI music from Repentance Plus
entry.summary: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance Plus was review-bombed on Steam after users found AI-generated music with Suno metadata in a GTA-themed segment; creator Edmund McMillen apologized, saying he had no idea. The incident highlights disclosure issues around generative AI in game development and Valve's disclosure requirements.

entry.title: I stopped talking to my husband and let AI do it instead. He didn’t even notice | Polly Hudson
entry.summary: A humorous personal column describing an experiment where the author answered her husband's texts using suggested AI replies, which went unnoticed. The piece is an anecdotal take on AI creeping into everyday communication via phone updates.
